newsitem.title: USA: NBA-NETS RE-SIGN POINT GUARD SAM CASSELL.
newsitem.headline: NBA-NETS RE-SIGN POINT GUARD SAM CASSELL.

text.p: Point guard Sam Cassell, who has been on four teams in the last year, re-signed with the rebuilding New Jersey Nets Tuesday.

Terms were not disclosed, but the New York Post reported Monday that the deal was for $21 million over six years, slightly less than what Cassell had been seeking when the free-agent market opened two weeks ago.

A year ago, Cassell was a member of the Houston Rockets, with whom he won NBA championships in his first two seasons. He was involved in three trades totalling 20 players, moving to Phoenix and Dallas before landing in New Jersey on February 17 in a nine-player deal, the biggest in NBA history.
"One thing I learned is anything can happen," the 27-year-old Cassell said. "I'll just prepare to stay in Jersey, win some games and go from here."

Cassell averaged 15.9 points and 5.0 assists in 61 games last season. He flourished with the Nets, averaging 19.3 points and 6.9 assists in 23 games before missing the final six contests with a pulled left hamstring.

"I was very adamant about re-signing Sam Cassell," said Nets executive vice president and coach John Calipari. "He is a leader and makes things happen. He has coachability as far as his relationship to me. He has great talent, great courage on the basketball court."
"My relationship with Cal is great," Cassell said. "He gives me the freedom to play my style of game."

Cassell was considered the top free-agent point guard available but his bargaining power was hurt by the fact that most teams had very little salary cap room. The Charlotte Hornets, one of the few teams with significant cap room and in need of a point guard, spent their money on David Wesley.
"Hopefully we can start winning, because this losing thing is old for me," Cassell said. "Hopefully we can get this thing turned around and win some more games."

Cassell was a 1993 first-round pick of the Rockets and helped them win NBA titles in 1994 and 1995. He played another season with Houston before being traded to Phoenix with three others for Charles Barkley.
In December, Cassell was dealt to Dallas in a six-player trade that sent Jason Kidd to the Suns. Two months later, he joined the Nets as part of a nine-player deal.
Cassell has averaged 11.4 points and 4.4 assists in his NBA career.

He returns as part of a young team that also features promising guard Kerry Kittles, swingman Kendall Gill and forward Keith Van Horn, the second pick in this year's draft acquired in a trade with Philadelphia. The Nets could still use a quality centre to round out their starting five.
"I think the backcourt is set," Calipari said. "We may still have some things to do, but at that point we'll be done and that will be our team for three to four years."
